## Separate support-export observer

The0.2 fixture variant reuses the same protected imported native-world,35-row/recipe/three-force and literal-credit assertions while preserving the frozen0.1 keyboard/drag protocol. Compose current `control.lua`, `support-exports.lua` and the appropriate `info-exports-f200.json` or `info-exports-f210.json` as `info.json`; retain the original corrected preservation fixture and exact five-mod Base closure. It imports no MIR code or saved state. Existing public validation checks profiles; native helpers only unpack returned data for independent value/metadata comparisons. The observer reads and writes no export files or engine logs.

Use `remote.call("mir5-library-native-input", "prepare", ACTION)` before the actual owned Windows input click, then `check` with the same action after the event settles. Each successful check returns the exact bounded selectable preview string for external file comparison; it is not file-readback evidence. Use the existing hash-bound1280×720 actor and actual inspected button coordinates, never synthetic Factorio GUI events. Prepare calls preserve an existing active export tab so repeated previews and failure retirement can be observed without rebuilding them first.

| Ordered action | Native and external expectation |
|---|---|
| en-full | Actual full-export click; readonly text-box; valid existing MIRSET1; false/zero/metadata values; EN file equals preview plus one newline, DE/server untouched. |
| en-compact | Actual compact click retires prior preview; compact file/string and public validation; no settings/research change. |
| en-diagnostics | Actual Help export; EN bounded latest mir.log and full profile; guidance distinguishes engine log and sharing metadata. |
| de-full | German client's own full export/string/file and exported_by; EN/server untouched. |
| de-compact | German compact export; prior preview retired and other role files unchanged. |
| de-diagnostics | German diagnostic report/full profile; EN/server untouched. |
| en-foreign | First close MIR with actual Escape, then click the fixture-owned matching-name button; no MIR output or native/settings mutation. |
| en-full-before-failure | Restore a real successful EN full preview before the settings-path failure. |
| en-settings-failure | Preserve the original EN output, then make only its disposable settings destination unwritable; actual click must give a clear target-peer error without native/settings changes. Restore the control before continuing. |
| en-diagnostics-before-failure | Restore a successful EN diagnostic preview/report before the report-path failure. |
| en-diagnostics-failure | Preserve the original EN report, then block only its disposable mir.log destination; actual click must report the failure clearly. The preceding full settings write may succeed and remains valid; restore the control. |
| de-rejoin-full | Stop/rejoin only the owned DE client; unchanged player identity/native state and a new full export. |
| en-restart-full | After two explicit server-console exports and `checkpoint`, retain the closed restart save, stop clients before host, restart/rejoin both and make one new EN full export. |

The two server-console commands are `/mir-settings-export` and `/mir-diagnostics-export`; use existing private RCON custody without exposing credentials. Before the last action, `checkpoint` writes `mir5-library-support-exports-restart`. The last checked action writes `mir5-native-complete`; report remains read-only after load. The declared sequence has13 observed GUI clicks, five joins, two explicit server exports, two new saves and seven actual processes if the parent uses two hosts and the specified client lifecycle. No new research laboratory is claimed; original protected labs are reused under their existing receipts.

The corrected observer requires one of each named server command, from the server console only, after the DE rejoin/export and immediately before checkpoint; duplicate or early/post-load commands refuse. The console event must have an absent `player_index`; numeric zero does not stand in for that origin. This differs from the file writer's explicit server target zero. Join counters bind each role and phase: exactly one initial EN and DE, one DE rejoin at its declared action, then one EN and DE join after the saved-host restart. Initial and post-restart roles may arrive in either order. The observer remains `await-restart` until both post-load roles arrive, rejects duplicate/wrong-role/wrong-phase events, and reports all role/command counts for independent native-log readback. An aggregate count alone cannot close these obligations. Original0.1 behavior and prior0.2 source/container/profile identities remain preserved; corrected dispatch uses the separately pinned r03 record.

File targeting and I/O failures require separate actual server/EN/DE write-data roots and retained before/after manifests. A host-side GUI projection cannot establish a requesting peer's local write error: the observer records each projection and requires the target peer's actual message, screenshot and files to be read independently. Preserve all original outputs before any disposable path control, verify resolved paths remain inside the explicitly owned run directory, use no recursive cleanup and restore the exact controls afterward. A report-path failure may leave a successfully exported settings file. Never count an observer marker alone as an I/O or multiplayer-safe pass.

Keep original and failed receipts, actor identities, actual clicks, native headers/joins and all role-local exports. Verify exact file bytes/string round-trip, full/compact false and zero values through the existing codec/facade, latest-report overwrite/bounds/content and absence of unintended peer outputs. Check server-only startup headers separately for init/configuration and ensure ordinary load/rejoin alone does not rewrite them before an explicit export. The startup path cannot capture an OS-process launch or read factorio-current.log. This is functional qualification outside scored timings; final package hashes, all owned fixture containers, helper/actor/controller hashes, source saves, geometry and teardown/restoration still require binding by the native execution owner before dispatch.
